**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Display only: `row_job` appends the posted line's bytes verbatim and the new shell test asserts `job.text == row label`. Copy/save and labels are untouched.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in non-test code. `tokenize` is total (spans cover the line exactly, malformed and non-ASCII input tested). `row_job` guards span offsets with `line.get(..)` and falls back to the plain remainder, so a stale cache entry can only mis-colour, never change the text.
- Tokenization is cached per program, with an O(1) per-frame key.
- Layering is respected: UI-only, no new components, no dependency, no snapshot PNGs touched, and the structural twin test was added instead.
- Provenance line present. The decision file `docs/decisions/256-gcode-highlight.md` is in place. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #256`. The PR touches no process files, `build.rs`, scripts or `.github`.

**Local results, merged with main** (branch already contains upstream/main; macOS)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gcode` | 9 passed (5 tokenizer unit tests, 4 viewer tests including the new colour test) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=1` | 536 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `program_key` samples only the length plus the first and last 256 bytes, so an in-place edit of the same length in the middle of a very large program would keep stale colours until it changes. This is display only and already documented in the code comment.
- `gcode_highlight.rs` is 253 lines, and `pages.rs` was already over 400 lines (1916), growth is net +3.
- Palettes were not checked visually in a real window (as the PR body says).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 2a0102e891b6fcc82264b82ae90e91a385c1ed28 -->
Independent review (second pair of eyes after the author's own).

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

What looks good
- Display only: `row_job` appends exactly the line's bytes (spans, then the unspanned remainder from `at`), and the shell test asserts `job.text == posted line`. A stale or mismatched cached span can only skip colouring, never drop a character (`gcode_highlight.rs` row_job guards).
- `tokenize` is panic-free on arbitrary text: char-boundary-safe stepping, unterminated `(` runs to line end, no indexing; unit tests cover coverage-of-line, multibyte, `((`, `;`. Dialect lines (`%NAME G71 *`, `*` block ends, `#100`, `o` words, Sinumerik) fall into Plain/OtherWord/Number: cosmetic only, nothing is altered.
- Tokenization is cached per program (O(1) key per frame); no new dependency, no snapshot PNG touched, new module carries provenance, 253 lines.

Local results (merged with main a6bd69d8, trial merge clean)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD crates/ui): 537 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Notes (non-blocking)
1. Rows are still built for every line each frame (not virtualised, as before); a multi-section `LayoutJob` per row is heavier than the old single `RichText`, so a 100k-line program may cost more per frame than before. The PR says this was not exercised; worth a look with a big program, or a `show_rows` follow-up.
2. Colours are fixed hex palettes, not theme tokens, so they bypass the `contrast` gate and colour-vision modes. Meaning is not carried by colour alone (the text is identical), so this is fine; a contrast-ratio unit test over the two palettes would keep it so.
3. `program_key` samples only length plus the first/last 256 bytes; an in-place edit elsewhere with the same length would keep stale colours until the program changes at its ends. Mis-colour only.
4. Heidenhain `%NAME` colours `N` as a block number; cosmetic.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
